Q: How do I optimize my code to solve SAT with a Rubik's cube in O(n²)? A:

SAT is a well-known NP-complete problem. As such, there are no known polynomial-time solutions to it, much less O(n²) solutions. If you think you've found one, then you've done what the most brilliant minds in theoretical computer science have failed to do for many decades. Is it possible that you have done so? Yes, but history strongly suggests you have not. There are mountains of false claims of solutions to the P vs. NP problem (some claiming that they're the same and some claiming that they are not). So far, they have all been found to be fatally flawed.

Q: Convert SELECT query with LEFT OUTER JOIN related by multiple conditions using CodeIgniter's query builder A:

You can manipulate query with db class and pass LEFT OUTER param in join method, see below

$this->db->select("c.c_id, c.c_name, p.phone_no")
->join("Phone AS p", "p.p_flex_id=c.c_id AND p.g_id'='1' AND p.ct_id='3'", "LEFT OUTER")
->get("Company AS c")

Q: MySQL 'user_id' in where clause is ambiguous problem A:

You should be mention alias name of your column and assign to user_id like

SELECT user.*, user_info.* 
FROM user as u 
INNER JOIN user_info as ui ON u.user_id = ui.user_id
WHERE u.user_id=1

Q: Ambiguous field name between an alias and a field in the select list with name A:

i did it, i add alias to all departments tables. Thanks everybody! You help me =)

select id_teacher, fio, post, teachersanddepartments.id_department , d1.name_of_department, id_subject, name_of_subject, subjects.specific, subjects.id_department, d2.name_of_department,
    id_classroom, number_of_classroom, classrooms.specific, classrooms.id_department, d3.name_of_department, id_group, name_of_group, groups.id_department, d4.name_of_department,
    specifics, daytime, pair, NUMERATOR_DENOMINATOR, keyy, typekey
    from ((((classes join teachers using(id_teacher) join teachersanddepartments using(id_teacher) join departments d1 on d1.id_department = teachersanddepartments.id_department)
    join subjects using (id_subject) join departments d2 on d2.id_department = subjects.id_department)
    join classrooms using(id_classroom) join departments d3 on d3.id_department = classrooms.id_department)
    join groups using (id_group) join departments d4 on d4.id_department = groups.id_department)

Q: What is the maximum length an Intel 386 instruction without any prefixes? A:

On 80386 that would be 11 bytes:

  • Opcode: 1 byte
  • MOD/RM: 1 byte
  • SIB: 1 byte
  • Displacement: 4 bytes
  • Immediate: 4 bytes

The 2-byte opcodes are using the 0Fh instruction prefix which obviously is a prefix. (Editor's note: the escape byte is not a "prefix" in the same sense as rep or 66h-operand-size, since it can't be repeated and has to be contiguous with the second byte of the opcode.)

None of the 2-byte opcodes take an imm32 immediate, at most imm8 like for bts/btr/btc r/m32, imm8, so the point is moot anyway in terms of max instruction length.

Q: Ambiguous Column Name Even Though Column Name and Table are Declared? A:

One problem is that INNER JOIN was designed to generate duplicate columns in the result. This problem was solved in 1992 when the SQL standard introduced 'relational' join types that don't generate duplicate attributes:

SELECT OrderDetailID
  FROM OrderDetails 
       NATURAL JOIN Products
 WHERE SupplierID = 5;
